deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is cautious overall: 141 names sit on Hold versus 63 actionable Buys (17 Strong Buy, 46 Buy) and 44 Avoid, so value signals are selective rather than broad. Every name in the top-five list carries a Strong Buy headline but was adjusted down to Buy after overlays—chiefly free-cash-flow basis mismatches and, in several cases, earnings or dividend-coverage warnings. Four of the five leaders cluster in Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group, Morgan Sindall, Johnson Service Group), with ITV alone in Communication Services, which raises sector concentration if you build a basket from this run alone. A central limitation is that headline cheapness and yield metrics often rest on FCF figures that diverge materially across filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted bases (for example FirstGroup filing £362.6M versus company-adjusted £113.5M), so dividend and FCF-yield passes need manual reconciliation before sizing positions.

FirstGroup (FGP.L) ranks first on composite score (89%, sector-relative 87%) with 15/22 model passes and all five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) clearing, including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), and Earnings Quality. Key metrics are P/E 8.5, P/B 1.29, yield 4.2%, ROE 16.7%, and screen D/E 19% (with a leverage override noting Yahoo D/E 161% versus £137.7m filing-adjusted net debt after IFRS lease gross-up). Failures are mostly deep-value and moat screens (Graham Defensive, Net-Net, Schloss, Deep Value, Economic Moat, Financial Health on weak liquidity). Industrials concentration applies if paired with the other top names. Verdict: accumulate — persistent 14-week signal and broad cheapness/quality pass set, but size conservatively until you reconcile FCF (£362.6M filing / £302.8M screen TTM / £113.5M company-adj) and lease-adjusted leverage.

ME Group International (MEGP.L) posts 15/22 passes and composite 82% (sector-relative 88%) with P/E 8.2, P/B 2.33, yield 6.8%, and ROE 28.2%, passing Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Buffett Quality, and Financial Health while failing Lynch PEG (core growth 0.4%, PEG 22.54), Piotroski (6/9), and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion). Overlays flag interim EPS decline (3.9%), net FCF dividend coverage 0.84× versus management 1.68×, and statutory versus filing core EPS growth divergence (>300 bps). Same Industrials cluster as three other top picks. Verdict: watchlist — yield and quality screens look attractive on paper, but net dividend coverage below 1× and earnings/FCF definition noise warrant filing-level work before buying.

ITV plc (ITV.L) shows 15/22 passes, composite 81%, conviction 70%, and timing “accumulate” (RSI 43, ~10.5% below the 200-day MA) with P/E 11.7, P/B 1.53, yield 7.1%, and ROE 13.5%, supported by High Dividend Yield, Lynch PEG, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, and Financial Health. It fails Buffett Quality, Economic Moat (ROE, ROA, margins, leverage), and Piotroski F-Score (3/9), and carries FCF basis mismatch (filing £148M, screen TTM £211.9M, company-adj £187M) plus statutory 1.00× versus management 1.53× dividend coverage. Not part of the Industrials cluster but exposed to advertising cyclicality and structural media risk outside the screen. Verdict: accumulate — favourable timing overlay and dividend/value model stack, tempered by weak Piotroski and moat failures.

documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a global estate of self-service photobooths (Photo.ME) and unattended laundry (Wash.ME), with FY2025 record profit before tax of £78.2 million on revenue of £315.4 million (RNS annual results, 23 March 2026). The quantitative screen rates MEGP.L as a strong buy on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk (15/22 models, composite 82%, c.6.8% yield, P/E 8.2, ROE 28.2%), but overlays flag weak adjusted EPS growth, interim EPS decline, and statutory free-cash-flow dividend coverage below 1×. The valuation hook is a cash-generative, net-cash balance sheet funding laundry rollout and buybacks, against a debate over cyclical consumer softness (April 2026 France/trading update), photobooth regulation and equipment cycles, and whether FY2026 PBT guidance of £69–74 million marks a genuine step-down from FY2025.
documents.investment_thesis: For a value investor, ME Group combines a visible asset base (49,000+ vending units, long-dated site partnerships) with improving mix: laundry already contributed 46% of Group EBITDA in FY2025 and over half at H1 2026, supporting margin resilience even when Photo.ME vending revenue falls. The screen’s strong buy is grounded in rare breadth—five factor families passing, including Economic Moat (sole pass among screened UK Industrials peers), High Dividend Yield, FCF Yield, Buffett/Quality Value, and Financial Health—with modest leverage (debt/equity c.28%) and persistent signal (14 weeks, conviction 72%). Business quality in filings aligns with the quality bucket: FY2025 EBITDA margin 38.2%, net cash £26.5 million (excluding lease liabilities), and dividend growth (+9.5% to 8.64p) alongside an £18 million buyback. The tension is growth: adjusted/core EPS growth in the screen is near flat (~0.4%), Lynch PEG fails, Piotroski scores 6/9, and Earnings Quality fails on weak free-cash conversion—so the strong buy is a “quality income at a discount” story more than a growth compounder. Capital deployment (laundry capex, buybacks, >55% payout policy) should be weighed against H1 2026 net cash falling to £7.5 million and reduced interim dividend (3.60p, −6.5%).

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary: ITV plc trades on low multiples and a high dividend yield while the quantitative screen flags a persistent strong buy (15/22 models, ~81% composite). The equity story is no longer a simple integrated broadcaster: the agreed sale of Media & Entertainment (M&E) to Sky for up to £1.6bn reframes the listed entity as a global ITV Studios business plus a planned ~£950m capital return, subject to CMA/regulatory clearance expected around H2 2027. FY2025 results were resilient—flat group revenue, group adjusted EBITA down only 1%, and management-reported free cash flow of £187m—but statutory cash conversion weakened (65% profit-to-cash vs 83% in 2024) and linear advertising remains cyclical. The central debate is whether headline cheapness and the cash-return path outweigh execution risk on separation, loss of diversified UK ad earnings, and tight statutory dividend cover from operating cash flow less capex.
documents.investment_thesis: For a value investor, ITV combines classic UK “yield plus rerating optionality” with a corporate catalyst. The screen passes all five metric families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk): P/E ~11.7, P/B ~1.5, dividend yield ~7.1%, debt/equity ~52%, and Lynch PEG ~0.51 on ~23% earnings growth—while timing overlay suggests accumulate (RSI ~43, price below the 200-day moving average). Business quality is mixed but improving strategically: ITV Studios grew external revenue 10% in FY2025 with 28% of studio revenue from streaming platforms; ITVX drove 16% streaming-hour growth and 12% digital ad growth, with digital ~31% of total advertising revenue. Cost discipline (£253m permanent non-content savings since 2019; further £20m guided for 2026) supports margins despite TAR down 5% in FY2025. The screen’s quality/moat models fail (Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Piotroski F-Score 3/9)—consistent with mid-teens ROE, thin broadcast margins, and working-capital volatility—not a deep moat compounder, but a cash-generative restructuring story at a discount. The Sky transaction (RNS, 6 July 2026) crystallises balance-sheet optionality: ~£950m return (~25p per share) after separation costs, a £2.1bn minimum content supply agreement (2028–2032), and Love Productions bolt-on—while leaving a listed studios pure-play targeting 13–15% adjusted EBITA margins and ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA post-completion. FCF basis divergence matters: filing-aligned statutory FCF was £148m (Yahoo/filing cash flow statement) vs company-adjusted £187m cited in results; statutory OCF−capex implies ~1.0× gross dividend cover vs ~1.53× on management’s adjusted measure—yield screens pass, but dividend durability needs monitoring on a statutory basis.

documents.name: Morgan Sindall Group plc
documents.executive_summary: Morgan Sindall Group plc is a UK-listed partnerships, fit-out and construction services group whose recent results show record revenue, strong adjusted profit growth and a net-cash balance sheet, while the quantitative screen flags a **strong buy** on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk metrics (16/22 models; composite ~80%). The value case rests on low double-digit earnings yield, ~4% dividend with ~2.4× cover on filing-based free cash flow, high ROE and a Piotroski F-score of 8/9, set against a cyclical sector that rarely passes “moat” or deep-value screens. The central debate is whether Fit Out and public-sector-heavy Construction/Infrastructure can keep carrying earnings while Partnership Housing and Mixed Use Partnerships absorb capital and margin pressure from a subdued private housing market. The share price sits below its 200-day moving average with neutral timing, which may help entry but does not remove cycle risk.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MGNS combines **enterprising Graham-style valuation** (P/E ~10.5, P/B ~2.4, debt/equity ~18%) with **quality and cash attributes** that are atypical for contractors: year-end net cash of **£531m** (FY2025 RNS), average daily net cash **£368m**, operating cash conversion cited at **87%** of adjusted operating profit, and filing-aligned FCF of **£170.7m** (screen policy basis) supporting dividend growth (total dividend **158p**, +20% y/y). The screen passes five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk—and leads its industrial peer set on model count, consistent with a compounder-like track record (management cites ~**18% CAGR** in adjusted PBT over ten years in the FY2025 results statement).

Business quality in filing terms is not uniform: **Fit Out** is the profit engine (FY2025 operating profit **£139.9m** on revenue **£1,784m**, margin **7.8%**), while **Partnership Housing** and **Mixed Use Partnerships** invest heavily in long-dated public-sector regeneration (secured plus preferred-bidder workload **£19.1bn** group-wide at FY2025). That mix explains why screens reward earnings yield and financial health yet fail Economic Moat (contracting ROA/margin thresholds) and Graham Defensive (current ratio ~1.23). The strong-buy signal is therefore best read as **quality-at-a-reasonable-price in a cyclical name**, not net-net or defensive compounder. The screen’s FCF TTM vs filing mismatch (£141.5m vs £170.7m) is noted in the snapshot; primary filing cash flow supports the yield case but warrants consistency checks before sizing.

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run’s screen is selective (63 buy-tier names vs 141 hold, 44 avoid) and the deep-analysis layer shows a systemic scoring–filing disconnect: headline cheapness, yield, and dividend passes often sit on FCF figures that diverge materially across filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted bases (called out explicitly for FGP.L, ITV.L, MEGP.L, MGNS.L, JSG.L). That gap does not invalidate the rank order on paper, but it blocks high conviction on sizing until reconciliation—especially for MEGP.L, where gap-fill evidence supports ~0.84× statutory FCF dividend cover, an H1 2026 interim dividend cut, and a research verdict of watchlist despite strong memo grades. Buy-tier filing bodies look broadly healthy in the sampled coverage table (no `thin_filing_tickers`; only TW.L stands out at 12 total filings vs ~58–118 for peers), and nine FTSE memo snapshots are all `strong` with high source quality scores—yet learning-path probes flag that memo-file counts elsewhere can mask thin research (`thin_memo_counted_as_coverage`, euro_depth). rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=20%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
plan.summary: Next rebalance would target 3 equal-weight sleeve(s); leave 2 near-target holding(s).

tasks.title: Re-import euro ingest cron slots after cadence change
tasks.summary: After merging library ingest cadence changes, run import_cron_jobs --all (or euro/sprint/maintenance job keys) so cron-job.org gets Mon–Sat peak + daily off-peak slots and disables old weekday-only titles. Sprint ≤4×/day × 24; maintenance ≤4×/day × 62. GitHub schedule alone is best-effort.

tasks.title: Register ops-monitor 13:15 UTC catch-up on cron-job.org
tasks.summary: After merging email-deferral catch-up, run import_cron_jobs.py --job ops-monitor-catchup (or --all) so external primary fires daily 13:15 UTC. GitHub schedule alone is backup. Verify with gh run list --workflow=ops-monitor.yml.

tasks.title: Rotate CURSOR_API_KEY after suspected exposure
tasks.summary: If Cursor API misuse or GitHub secret exposure is suspected: revoke the key in the Cursor dashboard, set a new GitHub Actions secret (and any Cloud/cron copies), review odd workflow_run jobs, and confirm main workflow files were not planted. Prefer main branch protection so a stolen GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push exfil workflows.

tasks.title: Register daily GHA secret-hygiene cron on cron-job.org
tasks.summary: After merging gha-secret-hygiene.yml, run import_cron_jobs.py --job gha-secret-hygiene (or --all) so external primary fires daily 06:20 UTC. GitHub schedule alone is backup. Verify with gh run list --workflow=gha-secret-hygiene.yml.

tasks.title: Sync valid Cursor API key into GitHub Actions secrets
tasks.summary: When ftse-verify-key --key-source legacy fails but --key-source v2 succeeds (or GHA agent jobs 401): copy the valid User API key into GitHub Actions secrets CURSOR_API_KEY_V2 and CURSOR_API_KEY. Workflows prefer V2 via secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY_V2 || secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY. Cloud secrets alone do not feed Actions.

tasks.title: Review open ingest deviations and reprocess if needed
tasks.summary: When Automation → Ingest deviations shows open rows (IR exhausted or weekday cap with leftover IWB), inspect the ticker. Approve writes a 7-day intensive pin for the next euro slot; dismiss closes the row for 7 days. Do not auto-replace IR URLs — that stays a judged allowlist edit.

tasks.title: Override FCF auto policy only when majority/filing is wrong
tasks.summary: Ordinary buy-tier FCF mismatches auto-resolve (majority among screen/filing/company-adjusted, else filing-aligned OCF−CapEx). Write docs/data/research/<TICKER>/sources/fcf_bridge.json only as a residual override when that auto pick is wrong, or when so-what flags fcf_bridge_needed because no filing/company figure exists. question_outcomes.evidence: FY2025 preliminary accounts extract in `filings/bodies/29bdb56d3cedb539.txt` shows TAR −5%, digital revenue +10% (£614m), profit-to-cash 65%, working-capital outflow £196m, statutory net OCF £202m and capex £54m (implied statutory FCF £148m, consistent with Yahoo), and CEO-stated management FCF £187m. H1 2026 `filings/bodies/ir_d69d4fb0d60611c6.txt` / `db26438f6be61fe5.txt` cite ~£20m H1 TAR impact from LHF rules (Oct 2025), CMA review, expected Public Interest Intervention Notice, and possible Phase 2 to H2 2027. question_outcomes.question: Can the 7.1% yield and Piotroski 3/9 be reconciled with a credible Studios/advertising FCF path, or is the screen catching a value trap in a structurally shrinking linear TV profit pool?
